paired_comparison_on_holdout.note: The development-panel effect (-6 collision, +7 overtake vs paired BC) not only failed to transfer, it reversed sign. The per-scenario flip counts (5 fixed / 10 new) have the same magnitude and symmetry as the churn measured on all 46 development-panel checkpoints (mean 6.96 fixed / 6.67 new).

binding_conclusion: The best confirmed development actor (V1.1 U2, 15/353) carries no transferable improvement over paired BC. Its development-panel advantage is a selection artifact, as predicted by the churn hypothesis and by CHECKPOINT_DISTRIBUTION_ANALYSIS.json (observed minimum 15 vs expected minimum 14.5 of 46 noise draws).

Per the preregistered rule this verdict is final for the V1.x micro-LR line: the reduced 22-arm study produced no real improvement, and the line is closed. The two-week exploration outcome is a validated negative result, not a validated actor.
The austin_600_holdout33 panel is now spent for V1.x: no other V1.x checkpoint may be evaluated on it (one-shot discipline, global across devices A and B).
Deployment recommendation unchanged from BC: pretrained/end2race.pth remains the best-evidenced actor. posttrained V1.1 checkpoints must not be represented as improvements.

Consequence for in-flight work: the three running ALS-final seeds (16-update repeats of AH-H0-p50-wr) belong to the closed line; their continuation is a budget decision for the owner, but their results cannot be selected against the development panel under the analysis record's no-further-selection rule.
